tokens/tokens-duration            Motion duration primitives. Three bands: fast (micro-interactions), medium
                                  (entrance/exit), slow (continuous). Min/max variants derive from base × ratio. Of a
                                  theme's two `motion` knobs, `tempo` (0.75-1.5) scales every duration here; `character`
                                  leaves durations alone. A duration scale beats `tempo` for the bands it sets, and
                                  explicit `tokens` beat both. `tempo` leaves these unscaled: finger tracking, momentum,
                                  the rubber band, the on-screen keyboard, the press's onset delay, cancel distance and
                                  tap flash, hover-intent delays, gesture thresholds, Spinner's and Skeleton's loops,
                                  and the 200 ms Reduce Motion cap. - @astryxdesign/cli

                                  `character` sets `--ease-entrance` and `--ease-move`: `crisp` decelerates without
                                  overshoot, `expressive` overshoots slightly, and at `standard` both equal
                                  `--ease-standard`; `--ease-exit` keeps its own curve at every character. `tempo`
                                  leaves curves alone. A duration scale's own fields win over the knobs, and explicit
                                  `tokens` win over everything. No curve here shapes motion that follows a finger or the
